notes: No breadboard or separate jumper wires are used: the battery pack and motors have their own fixed leads, which are screwed into the controller board's terminal blocks.
Battery red lead goes to VIN and black lead to GND, as the manual requires. The battery pack is switched off while wiring.
Motors can go either way round, so the left motor is Motor B and the right motor is Motor A. The terminal labels in the photos are only partly legible, so the A/B assignment is inferred.

The board sits on the Pi's GPIO header, so the board's GPIO ports are header-sockets and the Pi's are header-pins. This fixes the incompatible header-pin to header-pin pairs. The manual says the board uses GPIO 7, 8, 9 and 10. Only those and one GND pin are modelled. Its other pass-through pins are ignored.
Which GPIO pin drives which motor terminal is not given, so no through-connections are modelled inside the controller board.
The header GND pin is taken as the Pi's GND.1. The exact GND pin is not shown.
The 4xAA battery pack is not in the catalogue, so it is a new type with POS and NEG leads and a built-in on/off switch.
